claim: Everything as code is a family of distinct practices covering infrastructure, config, environments, pipelines, analytics, and security — not a single unified practice.
quote: EaC used as an umbrella term to cover specific applications of the 'as code' framework. There are diminishing returns on converting other platform parts to EaC.

claim: HashiCorp Vault centralises secrets management with dynamic credential issuance, fine-grained auditing, and encryption as a service.
quote: A tool for secrets management, encryption as a service, and privileged access management

claim: External Secrets Operator syncs secrets from external providers (Vault, AWS, Azure) into Kubernetes Secrets without storing credentials in Git.
quote: External Secrets Operator reads information from a third-party service like AWS Secrets Manager and automatically injects the values as Kubernetes Secrets.

claim: Open Policy Agent is the cross-layer unified policy engine for cloud-native environments using the Rego language.
quote: OPA is an open source, general-purpose policy engine that enables unified, context-aware policy enforcement across the stack.

claim: Unleash is an open-source feature management platform with GitOps-compatible API-first design.
quote: Open-source feature management solution built for developers.

claim: The most reliable IaC maturity diagnostic is asking when production was last changed from a developer machine without a PR; recent answers indicate Level 2 regardless of structural improvements.
quote: The most reliable assessment: 'When was production infrastructure last changed from a developer's machine without a pull request?' Recent answers indicate Level 2 operations regardless of structural improvements elsewhere.

claim: At Level 5 IaC maturity, infrastructure is fully deletable and recreatable from scratch, with production deployments requiring no downtime and debugging possible without direct system access.
quote: Production deployments generally have no required downtime; infrastructure deletable and recreatable from scratch; debugging possible without direct system access.

claim: Only 13% of organisations currently employ compliance-as-code, while more than half still rely entirely on manual compliance audits.
quote: Only 13% of organizations currently employ compliance-as-code, while more than half of organizations are still relying entirely on a manual approach, according to the 2025 State of Continuous Controls Monitoring Report.

claim: 97% of security professionals had a confirmed breach or near-miss linked to a misconfigured tool in the past year.
quote: 97% of security professionals surveyed had a confirmed breach or near miss in the past year because of a misconfigured tool, according to Reach's Drift Research Report.

claim: 96% of organisations have secrets scattered across code, configuration files, and multiple environments.
quote: 96% of organizations have secrets scattered across code, configuration files, and multiple environments, creating near infinite exposure points.

claim: GitGuardian's 2026 State of Secrets Sprawl found nearly 29 million new secrets exposed on public GitHub in 2025, a 34% year-over-year increase, with CI/CD config files among the primary exposure vectors.
quote: GitGuardian's 2026 State of Secrets Sprawl report found nearly 29 million new secrets exposed on public GitHub in 2025, a 34% year-over-year increase, with CI/CD configuration files and build artifacts among the primary exposure vectors.

claim: Storing even encrypted secrets in Git is a poor practice; the correct model is to store no secrets in the Git repository at all.
quote: it's a terrible idea to store the secrets (credentials) in the git repository even encrypted.

claim: A complete policy-as-code stack runs at four distinct layers: pre-commit scanning, pipeline plan gating, cluster admission control, and org-level cloud guardrails.
quote: Most organizations deploy multiple layers: CI scanning (Checkov), pipeline enforcement (Spacelift/Sentinel), cluster admission (Gatekeeper/Kyverno), and cloud-level guardrails (SCPs/Azure Policy/GCP constraints). The question isn't which tool to pick but where gaps remain.

claim: Database schema changes that bypass GitOps break auditability and cannot be safely rolled back.
quote: Top Database Schema Migration Tools to Avoid Change Outage 2026 — covering Flyway, Liquibase, Atlas, and Bytebase for GitOps integration.

claim: Atlas takes a schema-based declarative approach where developers declare desired state and Atlas automatically generates the migration diff, similar to how Terraform manages infrastructure.
quote: Atlas is a database schema-as-code tool that takes the 'schema-based' approach. Developers provide Atlas with the source-of-truth schema in SQL, HCL, ORMs, or other supported languages, and Atlas plans the migration changes automatically.

claim: Database schema migrations can be integrated into FluxCD GitOps deployments using Kubernetes Job resources (init containers) running before the application deployment.
quote: database schema migrations can be managed as part of Flux CD GitOps deployments using init containers, Jobs, and migration tools like Flyway and Liquibase.

claim: Complete runtime config-as-code requires environment isolation, immutable production (no direct writes), and dry-run deployment in simulated environments before production.
quote: Enforce production immutability to prevent manual modifications. Tag configuration versions for incident rollback. Isolate environment-specific settings across dev, test, and production.

claim: ConfigCat feature flags can be integrated with GitOps workflows via Terraform, making feature flags part of the version-controlled infrastructure definition.
quote: Terraform lets you define infrastructure as code, making it easy to include feature flags as part of your setup. ConfigCat can be used in GitOps workflows with tools like Terraform and Kubernetes.

claim: SaaS multiplies the configuration surface in ways traditional infrastructure tools were not designed to handle, as each application has separate admin consoles and access models without centralised oversight.
quote: SaaS multiplies the configuration surface in ways that traditional infrastructure tools weren't designed to handle. Each application has separate admin consoles, access models, and security configurations that lack centralized oversight.

claim: The average ratio of developers to platform engineers to security professionals is at best 100:10:1 (DORA research), making manual security enforcement unsustainable at scale.
quote: The average ratio of developers to platform engineers to security professionals is (at best) around 100:10:1 according to DORA research.

claim: Google SRE defines a complete configuration system by four properties: philosophy (goal-connected options), mechanics (validation + VCS), safety (rollout + rollback), and usability (tooling visibility).
quote: rolling update strategy for updating software or configuration instead of updating every pod all at once prevents catastrophic failures. Configuration modifications require gradual deployment capability, rollback ability, and automatic safeguards against losing operator control.

claim: Practitioners warn that when configuration becomes complex enough to require a full programming language, the logic should move into the main program rather than the config layer, and that hidden dependencies between config generators create untraceable behaviour.
quote: if your config is so complicated that it warrants a full-blown language, the logic should go into the _main program_. Configs 'emitted by config_generator.py which always ensures the precondition for foo, but only if it's also generating prod_env.json at the same time' create mysterious interdependencies.
